paper.title: Multi-Armed Bandits with Local Differential Privacy

settings.name_in_paper: epsilon-LDP bandit model with bounded rewards in [0,1]
unmapped: Local differential privacy: agent only observes outputs of an epsilon-DP mechanism applied to each reward; privacy level epsilon known to the algorithm
settings.definition_quote: For $\epsilon > 0$, the bandit model is said to be $\epsilon$-LDP if i) there is an $\epsilon$-DP mechanism $M: \mathcal{D} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ and ii) $A^{t+1} \in \sigma(A^s, M(R^s): 1\leq s \leq t)$ for any time $t$.

settings.name_in_paper: epsilon-LDP bandit model with Bernoulli rewards (lower bound)
unmapped: Local differential privacy: policy only observes outputs of an arbitrary epsilon-DP mechanism applied to rewards

settings.name_in_paper: epsilon-LDP bandits with unbounded reward supports (i.i.d. sub-Gaussian noise)
unmapped: Local differential privacy with privacy level epsilon
noise identically distributed across arms (same sub-Gaussian distribution, mean zero, variance at most one)
settings.definition_quote: Assume that mean rewards, $\mu_1, \mu_2,...,\mu_n$, are bounded and have been rescaled to $[0,1]$. Also, for each arm $a$ and time $t$, we assume that the reward of the $t$-th pull of arm $a$ is $\mu_a + Z_a^t$, where $(Z_a^t,a\in[n],t\in\mathbb{Z}^+)$ are i.i.d. sub-Gaussian with mean zero and variance at most one.

source.label: Thm:LB
source.quote: Let $\epsilon > 0$ be given. Assume that the rewards of all arms follow Bernoulli distributions. The regret $R(T)$ of any $\epsilon$-LDP policy satisfies \liminf_{T\rightarrow \infty}\frac{R(T)}{\log{T}} \geq \frac{1}{(e^\epsilon - e^{-\epsilon})^2} \sum_{a:\Delta_a > 0}\frac{1}{\Delta_a}.

results.notes: Stated for any epsilon-LDP policy; the proof uses consistency (o(T^alpha) pulls) and argues non-consistent policies have omega(log T) regret. Theorem number inferred from \newtheorem counter (first theorem).

source.label: Thm:LDP-UCB-L
source.quote: LDP-UCB-L is $\epsilon$-LDP. Its distribution-dependent regret is at most \sum_{a:\Delta_a>0}\Big[\frac{8(1 + 4/\epsilon)^2\log{T}}{\Delta_a} + \Big(1 + \frac{2\pi^2}{3}\Big)\Delta_a\Big] = O(...), and its distribution-free regret (for $T \geq n$) is at most $O(\epsilon^{-1}\sqrt{nT\log{T}})$.

results.notes: Paper's n = K. Paper states T is not assumed known; treated as anytime.

source.label: Thm:LDP-UCB-L
source.quote: and its distribution-free regret (for $T \geq n$) is at most $O(\epsilon^{-1}\sqrt{nT\log{T}})$.

results.notes: Distribution-free part of the same theorem.

source.label: Thm:LDP-UCB-B
source.quote: LDP-UCB-B$(\epsilon)$ is $\epsilon$-LDP. Its distribution-dependent regret is at most \sum_{a:\Delta_a>0}\Big[\frac{8}{\Delta_a}\Big(\frac{e^\epsilon+1}{e^\epsilon-1}\Big)^2\log{T} + \Big(1 + \frac{\pi^2}{3}\Big)\Delta_a\Big] = O(...), and its distribution-free regret (for $T \geq n$) is at most $O(\epsilon^{-1}\sqrt{nT\log{T}})$.

source.label: Thm:LDP-UCB-B
source.quote: and its distribution-free regret (for $T \geq n$) is at most $O(\epsilon^{-1}\sqrt{nT\log{T}})$.

results.notes: The epsilon^{-1} dependence presumably relies on epsilon bounded (e.g. epsilon <= 1), since (e^eps+1)/(e^eps-1)=Omega(1/eps) only for small eps; recorded as stated.

symbols.c_s: universal constant from the Sigmoid lemma (c_s >= 0.0765/e)

conditions: noise i.i.d. sub-Gaussian across arms and time with mean zero and variance at most one

source.label: Thm:LDP-UCB-LS
source.quote: Replacing CTL in LDP-UCB-L by CTL-S, we get LDP-UCB-LS. LDP-UCB-LS is $\epsilon$-LDP. Its distribution-dependent regret is at most \frac{1}{c_s^2}\sum_{a:\Delta_a>0}\Big[\frac{8(1 + 4/\epsilon)^2\log{T}}{\Delta_a} + \Big(1 + \frac{2\pi^2}{3}\Big)\Delta_a\Big] = O(...), where $c_s>0$ is a universal constant. Its distribution-free regret is at most $O(\epsilon^{-1}\sqrt{nT\log{T}})$.

results.notes: Expression copied as stated; the 1/c_s^2 placement on the Delta_a term is as written.

conditions: noise i.i.d. sub-Gaussian with mean zero and variance at most one
